problem:
The asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{49}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}=1$ are$\,\,y=\pm $
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
a=\sqrt{49}=7,\,b=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{7}x.$
